bull.b: A 10-year, contracted 50 MW engagement with AMD (TCV $636M, ~$51M annual NOI) creates durable, predictable cash flows and high-margin operating-lease income. Over 2–6 months this materially de-risks revenue growth, supports financing, and converts development effort into long-term recurring NOI.

bull.t: Large Bitcoin treasury as funding optionality
bull.b: A sizable BTC treasury (~15,679 BTC) provides non-dilutive liquidity and strategic optionality to fund development and bridge cash needs. This reduces near-term reliance on equity, supports phased delivery, and improves the company’s ability to pursue project financing and tenant-backed structures.

Lowered CapEx per MW and Corsicana core-and-shell consolidation (50% more capacity for same core-and-shell CapEx) improve capital intensity and long-term returns. Better development economics reduce funding needs per MW and raise potential ROI on future lease rollouts and expansions.

bear.t: Negative operating and free cash flow
bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow increases dependence on external financing, BTC sales, or project financing to fund growth. Over several months this cash burn risks delaying builds, forces higher-cost funding, and limits flexibility to pursue opportunistic expansions or capital returns.

bear.t: Data center revenue is early-stage, low recurring mix
bear.b: Nearly all data-center revenue is one-time tenant fit-out today, with recurring operating leases only a small fraction. This delays transition to durable, high-margin lease cash flows and keeps margins and cash generation vulnerable until leases scale and convert to sustained operating-lease revenue.

Large mark-to-market swings on BTC holdings produce volatile GAAP results and can mask operating performance. This creates earnings unpredictability that complicates credit access, performance benchmarking, and investor assessment of underlying mining and data-center economics.
